name: Augments

hlido_opinion.headline: A focused MCP server that hands Claude Code real type signatures, prose docs and working examples for any npm package — not a curated list — so the model stops guessing from stale training data.
hlido_opinion.body: Augments does one thing and states it plainly: it is an MCP server that gives Claude Code types, docs and examples pulled from npm for any package, not a hand-curated subset. The value proposition is sharp and real — coding agents routinely hallucinate APIs or lean on outdated training data, and a tool that injects current type signatures and working examples at the moment of use directly attacks that failure mode (the site frames it as a clean 'before: guesses / after: type signatures, prose docs, working examples'). Setup is a single line (`claude mcp add -s user augments -- npx -y @augmnt-sh/augments-mcp-server`), which is exactly the low-friction path an agent user wants. The reasons it sits mid-STEADY rather than higher: the reviewed public surface is a single landing page, so there is little evidence of depth — how many registries beyond npm, how it handles private packages, version pinning, or rate limits — and there is no visible license, adoption signal, or independent benchmark on the captured surface. It is a promising, well-scoped utility whose ceiling here is set by how little the public page lets us verify.

tier_rationale: STEADY (73) because Augments targets a real, specific agent failure mode (guessing npm APIs) with a genuinely agent-native, one-line MCP install and an 'any package, not a curated list' scope. Held at the lower end of STEADY because the public surface is a single page with limited evidence of depth, no visible license or adoption signal, and unverified handling of private packages, versioning and rate limits.
what_it_does_well: Precisely scoped: current type signatures, prose docs and working examples for any npm package, injected over MCP
Directly attacks a real agent failure — hallucinated or outdated API usage from stale training data
One-line install into Claude Code (`claude mcp add -s user augments ...`)
'Any package, not just a curated list' — no gatekept allowlist
what_it_fails_at: Reviewed surface is a single landing page — little evidence of depth or edge-case handling
No visible license, GitHub star count, or independent adoption signal on the captured surface
Unclear handling of private packages, version pinning, monorepos and rate limits
Scope is npm-only on the evidence seen — no other registries or languages demonstrated
best_for: Claude Code users who want accurate, current npm type signatures and examples at generation time
JavaScript/TypeScript teams whose agents frequently misuse library APIs
not_recommended_for: Teams needing multi-language/multi-registry documentation coverage beyond npm
Users who require a documented license, SLA, or proven handling of private-package auth

compared_to.verdict_diff: Serena gives an agent structural/symbol context about your own codebase; Augments injects external npm package docs and type signatures. Complementary rather than competing — Serena for your code, Augments for the libraries it depends on.

Continue is a full open-source AI coding-assistant framework; Augments is a single-purpose MCP server feeding npm docs into an existing assistant. Continue for the whole assistant, Augments as a targeted context plug-in.
